# Realtime Avatar SDK

> Server-side SDK for Realtime Avatar: a live character your users can talk to over voice or
> video, who listens while she speaks — so she can be interrupted mid-sentence.

Install: `npm install realtime-avatar` (+ `-proxy` for framework adapters)
Runtime: Node >= 20. Zero dependencies. Server-only (it holds the API key).

## Start here
- [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md): the contract for using this correctly — the whole surface, plus
  the rules that are expensive to break. Read this before writing code.
- [libs/http-client/src/types.ts](./libs/http-client/src/types.ts): every public shape, one file.
- [README.md](./README.md): human-facing overview and the 30-second example.

## Packages
- libs/http-client (realtime-avatar): the server client, zero dependencies
- libs/proxy (realtime-avatar-proxy): Next.js / Hono / Express adapters
  that keep the API key on the server
- libs/tools (realtime-avatar-tools): browser tool plane — she calls your
  functions mid-conversation; a call has 2.5s to answer
- libs/browser (realtime-avatar-browser): browser audio — enableMicrophone()
  returns WHY the mic did not start (the macOS system denial is not the browser denial, and the
  address bar cannot fix it), attachRemoteAudio() plays her and surfaces a blocked autoplay.
  No React, no livekit-client dependency
- libs/contracts (realtime-avatar-contracts): runtime schemas for the wire
- libs/mcp (realtime-avatar-mcp): MCP server so an agent can read avatars,
  balance and the per-session bill directly. Read-only unless REALTIME_AVATAR_ALLOW_WRITES=1.

Every call is full duplex — she listens the whole time she speaks, so she can be cut off
mid-sentence. `mode` only picks the renderer: mode:"avatar" (the default) publishes video,
mode:"voice" is cheaper audio-only. There is no `duplex` option.

## Example apps (standalone, each with its own README)
Quickstarts — the smallest correct integration per stack:
- [apps/quickstart/nextjs-app-router](./apps/quickstart/nextjs-app-router): route handler +
  call button
- [apps/quickstart/python-fastapi](./apps/quickstart/python-fastapi): the same split in Python,
  plus session-history (transcript + tool calls) signature verification
- [apps/quickstart/canvas-tools](./apps/quickstart/canvas-tools): the client tool plane —
  `clientTools: true` server-side, `attachAvatarTools` in the page, four tools closing over a
  live canvas, and the return-now pattern for a tool slower than the 2.5s deadline. Note
  `parameters` is plain JSON Schema; an `inputSchema` registers and then shows the model no
  arguments
Demos — larger showcases:
- [apps/demo/coding-companion](./apps/demo/coding-companion): the client tool plane —
  `clientTools: true` server-side, `attachAvatarTools` in the page. She starts builds via a
  tool, a cheaper model writes one standalone HTML page, and she publishes it to a Cloudflare
  Worker — receipt + poll for both, because a build and a deploy each outlive the 2.5s tool
  deadline. The preview is `sandbox="allow-scripts"` with no `allow-same-origin`
- [apps/demo/pair-programmer](./apps/demo/pair-programmer): the same app in a different room —
  identical brief, tools and build engine, composited the way `terminal-tutor` composites
  (character full height in her own column, the app on glass in front of her). Kept as a PAIR
  with `coding-companion` on purpose, so the only variable is the layout. It also uses
  `realtime-avatar-browser` for the microphone and remote audio where the
  companion inlines the same logic, which is the shortest side-by-side of what that package is
  for. Its layout facts: a panel may overlap the character only into her mask fade, and the
  vertical stack is measured by `fit()` rather than guessed in CSS — a dock that wraps at
  400px wide put a button on top of the status line
- [apps/demo/livestream](./apps/demo/livestream): comments, gifts and hearts all ride one
  `lk.chat` topic — she performs to a crowd she cannot see
- [apps/demo/live-shopping](./apps/demo/live-shopping): the same room with a cart in it, where
  a sentence stops being a performance and becomes an offer. She is NOT ALLOWED TO KNOW THE
  PRICE: the catalogue lives on the server, her brief and her tool descriptions carry no
  figures, and each of five verbs returns the number she may then say. Every figure a tool
  returns is written to a ledger with the deadline of the fact behind it — a flash price dies
  with its server-stamped window, a stock count in 45s, a shipping time never — and her
  captions are checked against it, because the failure is not a model inventing a price, it is
  a model correctly quoting one that has since expired
- [apps/demo/math-studio](./apps/demo/math-studio): the tool plane held at a fixed six verbs
  however far the app grows. A tool per thing on screen dies on arithmetic — `MAX_TOOLS` is 32
  and `instructions` caps at 4,000 chars — so the manipulatives register with a curriculum in
  the page and what she is looking at reaches her through the tool RESULT, not the tool name
- [apps/demo/terminal-tutor](./apps/demo/terminal-tutor): she draws on the screen — boxes,
  circles and arrows over the line or key she is naming — while teaching vim and tmux from
  behind translucent glass. She NEVER sends a coordinate: `highlight` takes a name
  (`text:delay`, `line:14`, `pane:right`) and the page resolves it, because a model cannot see
  the page it is pointing at and will aim confidently at nothing. A miss returns the list of
  what is addressable, so the retry is a pick rather than a second guess
- [apps/demo/dating-rehearsal](./apps/demo/dating-rehearsal): a first date you practice on, and
  four tools that are all HIS call, not the page's. `rate_interest` drives a live meter,
  `mark_moment` pins a green flag or an ick, `end_date` walks him out, `write_debrief` writes the
  after-card — the same model being charming is the one deciding how it went, so nothing scores
  the conversation but him. State rides the tool call, never a transcript a meter could misread
- [apps/demo/persuasion](./apps/demo/persuasion): the win condition is the character's own
  judgement. She holds one absurd position and concedes only by calling a `concede` tool when a
  genuinely novel argument defeats her — there is no scorer and no keyword list, and the win never
  rides a sentence speech recognition could re-spell. `clientTools: true` at the mint is the gate
There is no archive folder: a superseded example is deleted, not parked, so everything under
apps/ is current and safe to copy from.

## The shape
Your client asks your backend to start a call; your backend calls this SDK and relays the
connection payload back; your client joins and renders her.

## Non-obvious rules (each observed, not theorised)
- The API key is server-only; the constructor throws in a browser runtime.
- Relay `call.raw` byte-for-byte. Wrapping or adding a key makes the browser client reject it.
- An avatar built from a still IMAGE renders a black video track while reporting `ready`.
  Use `createAvatarFromVideo`.
- `{ queued: true }` means all slots are busy. It is a queue, not an error.
- Call `syncClips()` after ANY clip change, or a new clip silently does nothing.
- Verify transcript webhooks over the RAW bytes; re-serializing breaks the signature.
- Call policy (instructions, context, maxSeconds, video, voice) is decided by YOUR server.
  Never populate it from a request body.
- A slot is held from the grant, BEFORE the room exists. On `pagehide`, beacon a route that
  calls `rta.endCall(sessionId)` — and only ever end ids your own server minted.

## Not provided
- Hosted tool execution — the platform never runs your tools. They run in YOUR page (the
  client tool plane, `clientTools: true` + `attachAvatarTools`) against a 2.5s deadline.
- A Python SDK — Python's half is plain HTTP; see the example.

## More
- Full documentation: https://realtimeavatar.ai/docs
